papers.title: AnyRank: Reliable Anytime Policy Ranking via Sequential Testing
papers.abstract: Due to the high cost of hardware experiments, robot policies are predominantly evaluated by comparing their empirical performance on a limited number of hardware trials. However, finite-sample statistical uncertainty can lead to erroneous conclusions, especially when ranking multiple policies using a fixed batch of evaluation data. We propose AnyRank: a sequential method for multi-policy ranking that (i) adaptively allocates trials to hard-to-separate policies, (ii) provides (partial) rankings at any stopping time while bounding the probability of an incorrect ranking, and (iii) optionally exploits prior information to prioritize hardware evaluations more efficiently. This prior information could be informed from expert intuition, a small set of held-out hardware evaluations, or from policy rollouts in a simulator or an action-conditioned video world model. Notably, the prior can be imperfect; while a strong prior can provide efficiency gains on hardware, any inaccuracies in prior policy rankings do not invalidate the statistical assurances of AnyRank. We achieve the aforementioned properties through novel theoretical contributions that combine sequential testing with multiple-hypothesis graphical testing approaches. Experiments in simulation and real-world policy evaluation benchmarks show that AnyRank requires up to 50% fewer hardware evaluations compared to existing statistically rigorous approaches, while guarding against the incorrect rankings produced by heuristic methods used by state-of-the-art benchmarks.

papers.title: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon Robotic World Models
papers.abstract: Autoregressive robot video world models based on discrete visual tokens remain unreliable over long rollout horizons. Retaining the entire generated history does not necessarily improve prediction quality. We investigate a possible memory-role conflict in Full Context decoding: persistent scene information, recent visual-action states, and stale generated history compete for attention despite their different predictive roles. This perspective motivates ReCAP (Receding Context with Anchor Preservation), a training-free context-scheduling method for long-horizon robot video world models. ReCAP keeps the pretrained tokenizer, world model, and visual decoder frozen. It preserves the initial scene anchor and a contiguous window of recent complete visual-action blocks while evicting older generated history. The schedule preserves within-block structure and temporal order, requires no additional modules or parameter updates, and bounds active-context growth independently of rollout length. We evaluate ReCAP on RT-1, BridgeV2, LIBERO-90, and CALVIN using frozen autoregressive world models. Across evaluated environments and horizons, ReCAP improves visual fidelity, action-conditioned consistency, and robot structure preservation relative to Full Context. On BridgeV2, it reduces LPIPS by 63.3%. In the system benchmark at H=64, it reduces the logical KV footprint by 73.3% and p50 latency by 6.51%. Attention analyses show increased attention to retained recent states, while history interventions associate larger amounts of stale context with higher prediction error. These observations are consistent with the memory-role-conflict hypothesis, although they do not isolate it from context-length and position-handling effects. Our results support inference-time context scheduling as a practical approach to improving long-horizon robot video prediction and computational efficiency without retraining.

papers.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning has shown superior sample efficiency by leveraging the learned latent dynamics either in the form of derivative-free planning/imagined rollout training or dynamics gradient-based policy updates. While these approaches achieve comparatively fast learning, they all suffer, to varying degrees, from issues of recurrent compounding errors, high inference-time latency, and instability in backward propagation through time (BPTT). In this work, we propose a model-based RL approach that uses the chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator to optimize the chunk actor without recurrent model invocation. Through the collaborative chunk-wise prediction of the world model and policy, we can generate H-step hypothetical rollouts in a single forward pass and directly optimize value expansion, avoiding the costly and unstable BPTT. We evaluate our method on 19 challenging high-dimensional humanoid tasks from HumanoidBench and deploy our method to the real-world for quadruped bipedal walking. papers.title: From Video to Vision: Learning Generalizable Humanoid Carrying from Human Motion
papers.abstract: Most existing approaches rely on video or motion-capture data for reinforcement learning (RL) training; however, all of these methods require an upper-level module to generate reference trajectories in real time. In object carrying tasks, the humanoid can only lift objects from designated locations along the reference trajectory, resulting in poor spatial generalization. Moreover, existing policies can only be evaluated inside a motion-capture studio. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MOVER}, a multi-stage, Teacher-Assistant-Student, RL training framework for humanoid object carrying. We first collect data from videos and employ GENMO and GMR to retarget the video data, combining this with data augmentation techniques to generalize the data across objects of varying shapes and sizes. In the \textbf{first stage}, building upon the DeepMimic \cite{peng2018deepmimic} motion-training framework, we train the humanoid to transport objects from specified locations along designated trajectories. In the \textbf{second stage}, we relax the tracking of the reference motion and adjust the reward so that the humanoid learns to transport objects from different positions. In the \textbf{third stage}, we apply a Dagger-PPO distillation method to distill away the proprioceptive position observations and reference joint position of the humanoid. This allows the deployed policy to operate without relying on global position information from a motion-capture system; instead, the humanoid can directly perceive the object's pose from its onboard RGB-D camera to complete the carrying task. We design a series of simulation experiments to compare the success rates across stages (Stages 1 vs. 2) and before versus after distillation. We further transfer the policy to a real humanoid, successfully transporting objects at varying positions in a motion-capture-free setting.

papers.title: InfraWorld: Motion-Aware World Modeling for Roadside 4D Occupancy Forecasting
papers.abstract: Roadside 4D occupancy forecasting predicts future semantic occupancy in a fixed infrastructure coordinate system. Roadside scenes are globally structured yet locally evolving, requiring comprehensive scene-level context while precisely modeling sparse localized motion. However, existing forecasting paradigms struggle to tackle both requirements. To address this limitation, we propose InfraWorld, a world model formulating roadside occupancy forecasting as selective state evolution. InfraWorld maintains a dense BEV state for the complete scene and persistent motion queries for moving regions, assigning complementary states to global context and local dynamics. Specifically, we propose Dynamic Query Initiation (DQI) to initialize queries in regions supported by motion in the observed history. During rollout, the dense state is updated through Long--Short Temporal Fusion (LST), which combines short-term adjacent-frame continuity with long-term motion trends to preserve stable context while capturing scene evolution. Motion-Aware Query Injection (MAQI) then refines the queries and injects confidence-weighted query information into corresponding BEV tokens, enabling targeted dynamic updates without perturbing global context. Together, InfraWorld concentrates predictive capacity on evolving traffic regions. Extensive experiments on the InfraOcc and Occ3D--nus datasets demonstrate that InfraWorld achieves state-of-the-art performance for roadside 4D occupancy forecasting while retaining its effectiveness under ego-centric settings. Code will be released.

papers.title: Learn the Dynamics, Enforce the Physics: Generative Latent Operators for High-Dimensional Beam Evolution
papers.abstract: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is indispensable for modeling beam dynamics in particle accelerators, but its computational cost limits many-query workflows, such as configuration exploration, virtual diagnostics, and controller design. We introduce GLOBE, a physics-constrained Generative Latent Operator for Beam Evolution, modeling the nonlinear, control-dependent, multiscale evolution of 3D beam--field dynamics covering $10^7$ spatial cells. GLOBE compresses beam--field states into a compact latent space and factors their evolution into two components. A control-conditioned neural operator learns the dominant dynamics, while an amplitude-normalized generative model captures the residual distribution, recovering fine-scale structures and conditional variations. GLOBE enforces field constraints by regime-specific, parameter-free operators: a Poisson solve reconstructs the electric field in the electrostatic regime, and a spectral projection imposes Gauss's law and a divergence-free magnetic field in the electromagnetic regime. On two high-resolution 3D particle-accelerator benchmarks, bunched-beam transport and plasma-wakefield acceleration, GLOBE lowers relative-$L_2$ error by 9\% and 13\%, low-frequency spectral error by 69\% and 51\%, and mid-frequency spectral error by 54\% and 20\% relative to the strongest baseline (DPOT), satisfies field constraints, and reduces hours of PIC simulation to a minute per rollout.

papers.title: Inverse Optimal Transport Modelling of Hidden Barriers to Secondary-School Access in Dispersed Rural Settlements
papers.abstract: Distance is observable, but the effective cost of secondary-school access in dispersed rural settlements is shaped by barriers that are partly hidden in enrolment and attendance flows. This study develops an entropic inverse optimal transport framework that recovers latent generalized access costs from origin–school flow matrices while respecting learner totals and school capacities. The model combines network distance with river crossings, road condition, safety exposure, transport fares and household–school compatibility. Existence, uniqueness, Sinkhorn representation, invariance, parameter identifiability, stability and accessibility bounds are established. A reproducible synthetic experiment with 24 settlements, five schools and 1,230 capacity-weighted places demonstrates the method without representing simulated observations as field evidence. The full inverse model reduced Kullback–Leibler flow error from 0.38579 for a distance-only specification to 0.00431 and recovered standardized barrier coefficients with an Euclidean error of 0.3157. River crossings and transport fares produced the largest non-distance penalties. A soft-min accessibility index translated the recovered cost surface into settlement priorities. Counterfactual transport subsidies and a hostel reduced both average and upper-tail generalized costs, whereas a candidate school-placement rule exposed an equity efficiency trade-off. The framework therefore converts routinely available origin–destination counts into interpretable planning evidence, while explicitly separating structural inference from causal claims. Field validation, uncertainty quantification and participatory specification remain necessary before operational allocation.

papers.title: Fermatean Fuzzy Model Predictive Control for Robot-Assisted Metaverse Rehabilitation Under Network Delay and Haptic Uncertainty
papers.abstract: This proof-of-concept numerical study examines a metaverse rehabilitation pathway in which a haptic device enables a patient avatar to perform a virtual task inside an edge-rendered therapy environment. The rehabilitation loop is sensitive to communication delay, haptic ripple, measurement uncertainty and varying patient fatigue. When the link goes unstable, a fixed controller generally responds too aggressively and when the patient regains smooth motion it can react too conservatively. In this regard, the paper formulates a Fermatean fuzzy model predictive controller (FF-MPC) that updates its state penalty, control penalty and admissible assistive force at each slot. The method does not rely on a large corpus of linguistic rules. Instead, a compact algebraic map converts normalized tracking error, round-trip delay, force ripple and fatigue into a Fermatean tuple and then into a Fermatean risk index used by the receding-horizon controller. A synthetic numerical study was designed for a shared metaverse rehabilitation room with a 20 ms sampling interval, a two-state arm model, bounded assistive force, and delay conditions from 20 to 80 ms. Four controllers were compared: proportional-integral-derivative control, fixed model predictive control, type-1 fuzzy MPC, and the proposed FF-MPC. At 60 ms mean delay, the proposed controller reduced position root-mean-square error from 39.6 mm to 22.4 mm, reduced the peak interaction-force statistic from 22.7 N to 14.4 N, and reduced the passivity-violation rate from 24.7% to 8.6%. The worked numerical example also shows how the proposed method converts a single measured state into adaptive weights Qk = diag113.53,25.15, Rk = 0.0940, and an assistive action of 1.94 N. Across all uncertainty levels, the proposed controller stayed the most compact in phase space and reached the lowest mean stage cost.

papers.title: An accurate low-order model of a fin-and-tube heat exchanger for the dynamic simulation of heat pumps
papers.abstract: Dynamic modeling of heat exchangers is essential for the analysis, control, and optimization of vapor compression systems such as heat pumps and air conditioners. These technologies are increasingly relevant in the context of energy transition, where regulatory frameworks and climate goals demand improved energy efficiency and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Accurate yet computationally efficient models are crucial for system-level simulation, control design, and digital twin development. Traditional low-order approaches, such as lumped parameter and moving boundary models, offer fast computation but often lack the fidelity needed to capture dynamic two-phase phenomena, especially under transient or off-design conditions. Finite volume models offer better accuracy but are often too computationally demanding for real-time applications. This work presents a segment-by-segment heat exchanger model that balances accuracy and efficiency, allowing for detailed prediction of dynamic behavior with limited computational cost. The model was implemented using the Simscape language within the Simulink environment and was validated in both condenser and evaporator configurations. Simulation results show good agreement with a higher-fidelity reference model developed in EVAP-COND 5.0 environment, with a maximum deviation of 2.7% for the sensible heat transfer in condenser mode, while the evaporator mode exhibited deviations of 6.8% for the latent heat transfer and -2.4% for the sensible heat transfer. The proposed approach supports the development of advanced, energy-efficient HVAC systems within increasingly stringent regulatory contexts.

papers.title: Experiential Learning Strategies In Teaching Araling Panlipunan and Students' Cognitive Skills
papers.abstract: Experiential learning provides meaningful real-life experiences that support students’ cognitive skills in Araling Panlipunan. This study examined the relationship between experiential learning strategies and students’ cognitive skills in the South Bukidnon District for School Year 2026–2027. Specifically, it assessed teachers’ use of role-playing and simulations, community-based learning, reflective activities, and problem-based learning, and students’ cognitive skills in analysis, evaluation, and problem-based reasoning. The study involved 150 Araling Panlipunan teachers and 300 corresponding junior high school students selected through two-stage sampling: purposive sampling for teachers and simple random sampling for students. Using a descriptive correlational design, validated researcher-made questionnaires were employed. Mean and standard deviation described the levels of experiential learning strategies and students’ cognitive skills, while Pearson Product-Moment Correlation Coefficient tested their relationship. Multiple linear regression determined whether experiential learning strategies significantly predicted students’ cognitive skills. The findings showed that experiential learning strategies were implemented at a very high level, with community-based learning obtaining the highest mean and role-playing and simulations the lowest. Likewise, students’ cognitive skills were at a high level, with problem-based reasoning emerging as the highest dimension and evaluation as the lowest. Significant positive relationships were found between experiential learning strategies and students’ cognitive skills. Multiple linear regression also showed that experiential learning strategies significantly predicted students’ cognitive skills, with problem-based learning emerging as the strongest predictor. The study concludes that experiential learning is meaningfully associated with students’ cognitive development in Araling Panlipunan. It recommends strengthening active learning experiences and students’ ability to assess issues critically.

papers.title: Tool Performance and Multi-Response Optimization of SLM-Fabricated Ti-6Al-4V Using Coated Carbide Tool for Marine Applications
papers.abstract: Titanium alloys are distinguished by their exceptionally high strength-to-weight ratio, which is unaffected by the hightemperatures at which they are used. Because of this property, they are suitable for a wide range of different marineapplications. Titanium alloys have an exceptionally high corrosion resistance. The defects that arise may influence the part’s functionality in some way. In the present research, the fabrication of powdered Ti-6Al-4V into a rod using Selective Laser Melting (SLM) and its machining were carried out with coated carbide tools, as is customary in the marine industry. As well, the morphology of both the powder at 50 μm and the rod surface at 10 μm has been discussed in brief. The workpiece at varying speeds and feeds, the tool wear and surface roughness that resulted from the process have also been examined, along with Taylor’s tool life analysis, and Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) have also been provided.

papers.title: From wetting-front coalescence to urban road collapse: interpretable machine learning of hydro-mechanical failure under coupled rainfall and pipeline leakage
papers.abstract: Abstract Urban ground collapse poses a severe threat to public safety, road operation and underground infrastructure in densely developed cities. This study investigates the hydro-mechanical failure mechanism of road collapse induced by coupled rainfall infiltration and pipeline leakage through physical model testing, finite element simulation and interpretable surrogate modelling. A validated numerical model incorporating saturation-dependent strength and stiffness degradation was used to generate 120 cases with different pipe burial depths, rainfall intensities and leakage pressures.The results indicate that collapse develops through shallow-soil pre-wetting, leakage-induced wetting-zone expansion, convergence of the upper and lower wetting fronts, and upward propagation of deformation. Leakage pressure is the dominant factor, contributing 86.42%, 87.79% and 92.77% to the variations in collapse depth, near-saturated zone area and wetting-front depth, respectively. Rainfall mainly dissipates matric suction and lowers the failure threshold, whereas burial depth regulates the wetting-front convergence and deformation-transfer path. GPR/Kriging achieved test-set (R 2 ) values of 0.997–0.998, while XGBoost-SHAP confirmed the mechanism of leakage-pressure domination, rainfall amplification and burial-depth regulation. Risk zoning further shows that increasing rainfall shifts high-risk conditions towards lower leakage pressures, particularly at intermediate burial depths. The proposed framework provides an efficient tool for identifying vulnerable pipeline sections and supporting targeted inspection and collapse prevention.

summary_en.motivation: Urban road collapse driven by coupled rainfall infiltration and pipeline leakage involves complex hydro-mechanical mechanisms that are costly to simulate at scale.
summary_en.method: Physical model tests and finite element simulations generated 120 cases, which were then used to train GPR/Kriging surrogates and interpreted via XGBoost-SHAP.
